summary: Bazaruto Island Airport serves the stunning Bazaruto Archipelago off the coast of Mozambique, one of Africa's premier beach and marine destinations. This small regional airport is the primary gateway for visitors heading to the island's luxury lodges and national park. Its remote coastal location makes air travel the most practical way to reach the archipelago from the mainland.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Bazaruto Island Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves tourists visiting Bazaruto Archipelago National Park and the island's luxury resorts, as well as a small number of local residents.

Q: How do I get to Bazaruto Island from the airport?
A: Most resorts provide boat transfers from the airport area to their lodge locations on the island. Transfer times vary depending on the resort's position along the coast.

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to BZB?
A: The airport is mainly served by charter and small scheduled flights, typically connecting through Vilankulo on the mainland.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Facilities are minimal given the small size of the airport; travelers should expect basic services and are advised to arrange ground transport in advance.
transport_tips: Most visitors fly into Vilankulo Airport on the mainland and then take a short connecting flight to BZB. Resort transfers by boat are typically pre-arranged, so confirm pickup details with your lodge before arrival. There are no public buses or taxis serving the airport, so independent transport options are limited.
local_tip: Pack motion sickness remedies for the boat transfer from the airstrip to your lodge, as waters in the channel can be choppy depending on tide and weather conditions.
